resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. student_facing §9 (judge-owned look-line criterion) line 31: harm: I read the exercise, the §9 text in check_student_facing.md (line 87), and prompts personal-agent-homework-1 and -3. The finding fails on four points.

1. L31 object and tell are carried elsewhere. "Spot-check both" refers to style.md and the one CLAUDE.md line. Prompt 1 makes the agent "Show me both files before saving", so the student is reading an artifact, not the agent's account of a fact. §9's object clause ("the agent's account of X rather than X") has no bite here, because the files are the things under inspection, like the diff the rule calls fine. Prompt 1 also defines good output in the same view: hex codes, font families, and "a designer reading ./style.md should be able to produce something that looks like our site without visiting it". The tell is also partly in the sentence itself ("Add any hard brand rule the agent missed ('never pure black,' 'always serif headings')"). That part is a direct "you do it" step, which the §9 carve-out (Antti 2026-09-06) accepts.

2. The L53 tell is carried by Phase 2 and Phase 5. Phase 2 L25-27 says "Give your daily output the look of your company's website". Phase 5 L63 says "Styling drift from your company site: sharpen ./style.md". Together these tell the student to compare the page against the company site, and the response is named. L53 itself is a do-line ("Double-click ... To fix anything, edit ..."), not a bare look-line.

3. The proposed fix cuts against §9. The fix has the student hand-check that style.md contains hex codes and named fonts and that CLAUDE.md gained exactly one line. That is more manual error-catching, which §9's first half bans (replace it with "ask the agent to audit its own work"). §9 also says "the fix is never more words", and two prior cards were declined as "longer with very little value add". The proposal adds a clause at L31 and a clause at L53. It also moves the Claude-over-abstraction and "first render ignores style.md" watch-fors out of the maintainer block. That block deliberately defers them ("Deferred per student-facing-first rule", L97), alongside the sibling note at L98 ("HTML-doesn't-look-native ... neither belongs in the exercise body").

4. Part of the harm claim is unsupported. The judge says "The student can catch both in the moment". L97 itself says the student "sees generic and doesn't know the style.md wasn't read", so a student may not catch it. I concede one real residual at L53: the maintainer block shows a generic first render is a plausible failure. A single short clause there could be defended. That is optional polish for one line, not a BLOCKING finding on L31, and not the bundled fix proposed. I checked the judge's factual claims. Line numbers, quotes, and the contents of the maintainer block all match, so no count is wrong. The judge's reading of the rule as a blocker is the part that does not hold.
